hook: Reis-Filho built his career deciphering cancer genomics at the bench, at the Institute of Cancer Research and then as Chief of Experimental Pathology at Memorial Sloan Kettering, before moving to AstraZeneca to apply AI foundation models and agentic frameworks directly to drug discovery and clinical development, one of the clearer examples of a working oncologist becoming an enterprise AI leader.
name: Jorge Reis-Filho

quote.text: Our focus includes developing advanced foundation models and agentic frameworks, strategically crucial technologies aligned with AstraZeneca's bold ambition.
quote.context: Jorge Reis-Filho, personal LinkedIn profile summary

moniker: Chief of AI for Science Innovation at AstraZeneca

reading.body:
Jorge Reis-Filho's career trajectory is one of the cleaner data points available on how deep domain expertise in cancer biology is becoming a direct pathway into enterprise AI leadership, rather than a parallel track to it.

His timeline moves from molecular pathology benchwork in 2006, through academic leadership at the Institute of Cancer Research and Memorial Sloan Kettering, to a vice president role in cancer biomarker development at AstraZeneca in 2023, and then to Chief of AI for Science Innovation in 2025. The two-year gap between those last two titles is notable: it suggests AstraZeneca structured a deliberate on-ramp, putting a scientist with genomics and big-data experience into a commercial biomarker role before handing him responsibility for foundation model and agentic framework deployment across the drug discovery pipeline. His advisory work at Paige.AI, which contributed to FDA clearance of a computational pathology product, provided additional applied AI exposure outside his primary employer.

The data covers his roles, awards, and stated focus areas, but does not describe the scale of compute infrastructure underlying AstraZeneca's foundation model work, the specific models in use, or how the enterprise AI unit is organized beneath him. What it does establish is the professional archetype: a researcher who accumulated two decades of experience in the biological problem space, moved into translational and commercial settings, and arrived at an AI leadership position carrying both the domain fluency and the institutional credibility that purely technical candidates would lack.
